newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: India tenders to sell 140,000/T May, June naphtha.
newsitem.headline: India tenders to sell 140,000/T May, June naphtha.

text.p: State-owned India Oil Corp (IOC) has issued several tenders to sell low aromatic (LAN) and high aromatic naphtha (HAN) for May and June loading, industry sources said on Tuesday.

IOC has issued tenders to sell 27,000 tonnes of LAN for loading May 27-29 loading from Madras, on the east coast and 30,000 tonnes of LAN also for similar date range loading from Bombay on the west coast.
It has also tendered to sell a 25,000 tonnes of HAN for June 5-7 loading from Bombay.
Traders said these tenders will close May 15 and are valid for one day.

This is in addition to 30,000 tonnes of HAN and 25,000 tonnes of LNG for May 25-27 loading from Cochin and Hazirah respectively, issued a week ago. These tenders will close May 16 and are also valid for one day.
Traders said India's tender to sell 28,000 tonnes of LAN for May 17-19 loading which closed May 9 has been deferred due to poor response. The tender's closing date has been postponed to May 14.
In its last tender, IOC sold 30,000 tones of HAN at a record low price of around $40 a tonne below Japanese spot quotes for May 6-7 lifting free-on board Cochin.
Traders in India told Reuters that exports of naphtha and LNG in May and June totalling 165,000 tonnes are due to refineries resuming operations after the recent scheduled maintenance shutdowns.
A trader in Singapore said some refineries in India have also increased their throughput and have been running more sweet crudes resulting in the surplus naphtha.
